Messages.Author: Peter Gordon WILSMORE
Messages.Body:
how are unique masters contested? i only remember rules about contesting
master: unique locations and titles. can unique equipment be contested? if
so how? can anyone point out where in the rules it says this
--
Peter Gordon WILSMORE, cs95...@cs.uwa.edu.au, First Year Student

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
In article <cs959651-120...@130.95.80.133>,

Peter Gordon WILSMORE <cs95...@cs.uwa.edu.au> wrote:
>how are unique masters contested? i only remember rules about contesting
>master: unique locations and titles. can unique equipment be contested? if
>so how? can anyone point out where in the rules it says this

All unique *cards* are contested in the same way: a Methuselah pays a pool
during untap to continue contesting the card or she may elect to burn the
card. This includes *all* unique cards: Vampires, unique Allies/Retainers,
Unique Masters, Unique Locations, Unique Equipment, etc.
This is describe under section 8, which never makes any reference to
locations.

Titles are not cards and are Contested in a different way. [17.2]

Messages.Author: James R. McClure Jr.
Messages.Body:
cs95...@cs.uwa.edu.au (Peter Gordon WILSMORE) wrote:
>how are unique masters contested? i only remember rules about contesting
>master: unique locations and titles. can unique equipment be contested? if
>so how? can anyone point out where in the rules it says this

Peace Peter,

All unique things (except vampire titles [Prince of Foo or Foo Justicar]) are
contested in the same way. When a second (or subsequent) copy of the Unique
Thing comes into play, all copies of the UT are "contested." This has the effect
of removing all copies of the UT from the game (are not affected by any cards
which do not explicitly state that they affect contested cards). During the
Untap Phase of each Methuselah who lost control of a copy of the UT, that Meth
may either 1) "contest" - that is continue to oppose all other Meths for control
of the UT or 2) "yield" - that is cease opposing all other Meths for control of
the UT. When you "contest", you pay one pool for each UT that you are contesting
control of. When you "yield", you burn that copy of the UT (and all cards that
the UT directly owns [equipment/retainers]). When only one Meth remains with
a copy of the UT "in contestment" and that Meth's Untap Phase rolls around, that
Meth returns the UT back to play and may utilize the UT immediately (as appropriate).
Contesting vampire titles works the same way, except: 1) only the title [not
represented by any card] it removed from play; 2) the vampires who had possessed
the contested title pay one blood each Untap Phase to "contest"; 3) a vampire in
torpor must yield.

I hope this helps.
